title: Commodities Brief — 18 Nov 2026
intro: Commodities are enduring a broad-based liquidation during the Asian session, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Gulf and risk-off sentiment spilling over from equities. The US dollar index is higher at 103.75 alongside a firmer 10-year yield of 5.103%, weighing heavily across the complex.

sections.heading: 🛢 Oil desk
sections.content: Crude benchmarks are sliding sharply with WTI at 84.16 down 2.15% and Brent at 91.90 down 1.33% on the day, leaving the Brent-WTI spread wider at 7.74 dollars. The sell-off accelerates as Iranian military actions target US drone and missile sites in Kuwait, compounding regional supply fears while broader financial markets face severe disruptions. The front curve remains under intense pressure as risk premiums contend with broader macro liquidations.

sections.heading: Natural gas & products
sections.content: Natural gas edges lower to 3.187 down 0.65%, while refined products drop steeply with RBOB gasoline at 2.465 down 2.77% and heating oil at 3.933 down 2.83%.

sections.heading: Metals
sections.content: Precious and industrial metals are nursing heavy losses led by copper at 5.785 down 3.20% and silver at 45.79 down 3.17%, while gold pulls back to 3,768.70 down 2.47%. Stronger US yields and a firmer DXY are compounding the downside pressure across the metals complex despite industrial demand concerns.

sections.heading: Agriculture
sections.content: Grains are mixed as wheat rises 1.30% to 603.00 while corn and soybeans edge lower, and softs remain subdued with coffee down 0.27% at 279.95.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▼ Bearish · WTI — below 83.50 opens 80.50 · invalid above 85.50*
Broad risk-off liquidation and rising US yields accelerate selling pressure below key support.
- *▼ Bearish · Brent — below 91.00 opens 87.50 · invalid above 93.50*
Macro headwinds and broader commodities sell-off weigh on international crude benchmarks.
- *▲ Bullish · Wheat — above 610.00 opens 630.00 · invalid below 595.00*
Relative resilience and positive weekly momentum attract buyers against the broader trend.
- *▼ Bearish · Copper — below 5.700 opens 5.450 · invalid above 5.900*
A stronger dollar and risk aversion drive deeper liquidation in industrial metals.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Escalation of military conflict in the Gulf and potential disruptions to regional energy infrastructure.
- Macroeconomic volatility surrounding the upcoming FOMC meeting minutes and wider financial system outages.
